explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/713, second question: if ex(n;G) ~ c n^α for a bipartite G (α ∈ [1,2), c > 0), must α be rational? The Lean statement: for every bipartite G on Fin q with at least two edges and every α ∈ [1,2), c > 0 with extremalNumber n G ~ c·n^α, α is the image of a rational. Since such α is unique when it exists, this is the positive form of 'must α be rational', decoupled from part (i)'s existence question. The ≥ 2 edges condition only excludes degenerate G (≤ 1 edge) with ex(n;G) eventually 0, for which no such asymptotic can hold anyway; small examples (2K₂, P₃, forests) give α = 1. Faithful.
